answer_text:
Let

\[
I=\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\left(\int_1^{\sqrt{x}} e^{-t^2}\,dt\right)dx.
\]

Use the substitution

\[
u=\sqrt{x},\qquad x=u^2,\qquad dx=2u\,du.
\]

When \(x=0\), \(u=0\); when \(x=1\), \(u=1\). Also,

\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}dx=\frac{1}{u}(2u\,du)=2\,du.
\]

Thus

\[
I=\int_0^1 2\left(\int_1^u e^{-t^2}\,dt\right)du
=2\int_0^1\int_1^u e^{-t^2}\,dt\,du.
\]

Since \(0\le u\le 1\), we have

\[
\int_1^u e^{-t^2}\,dt=-\int_u^1 e^{-t^2}\,dt.
\]

Therefore,

\[
I=-2\int_0^1\int_u^1 e^{-t^2}\,dt\,du.
\]

Now change the order of integration. The region is

\[
0\le u\le 1,\qquad u\le t\le 1.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
0\le t\le 1,\qquad 0\le u\le t.
\]

So

\[
I=-2\int_0^1\int_0^t e^{-t^2}\,du\,dt
=-2\int_0^1 t e^{-t^2}\,dt.
\]

Now evaluate the remaining integral:

\[
\int_0^1 t e^{-t^2}\,dt.
\]

Let \(v=t^2\), so \(dv=2t\,dt\). Then

\[
\int_0^1 t e^{-t^2}\,dt
=\frac12\int_0^1 e^{-v}\,dv
=\frac12(1-e^{-1}).
\]

Hence

\[
I=-2\cdot \frac12(1-e^{-1})=e^{-1}-1.
\]

\[
\boxed{e^{-1}-1}
\]
